title: Marked proper curve deformations and square-zero operation relations
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $K$ a field [def-weil-field], $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$, and $X$ a proper curve family over $\operatorname{Spec}K$ in [def-sfb-proper-curve-moduli]. Work in its universe convention, with algebraic spaces as in [def-trf-algebraic-space] and the chosen sheaf fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. For a $K$-vector space $M$ with its central right $K$-action, let $D_M=\operatorname{Spec}(K\oplus M)$, using the split square-zero algebra [def-sc-trivial-square-zero-extension], with reduction $i_M:\operatorname{Spec}K\to D_M$ and projection $p_M:D_M\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. A linear map $M\to N$ induces $D_N\to D_M$ by the corresponding algebra homomorphism. When $M=K$, use the dual-number base $D_K$, reduction and projection already defined in [def-sfb-proper-curve-moduli]. A marked deformation along $i:\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ is a proper curve family $Y/T$ with a cartesian arrow $X\to Y$ over $i$, equivalently a specified identification of its special fibre with $X$. Two marked deformations are isomorphic when an isomorphism over $T$ commutes with their marking arrows. A marked deformation is the base change of another along $b:T\to U$ when the two reduction maps satisfy $b\circ i=j$ and there is a cartesian arrow over $b$ commuting with the markings. Define $T_X$ to be the quotient of marked deformations over $D_K$ by isomorphism. Define the zero relation to mean the class of the trivial family $X\times_KD_K$ with its canonical marking. Define the scalar relation $s=ct$ to mean that representatives of $s,t$ are related by cartesian pullback along $D_K\to D_K$ induced by $(b,m)\mapsto(b,cm)$. Define the addition relation $r=t+s$ by the existence of a marked proper curve family over $D_{K\times K}$ whose restrictions along the two projections on directions represent $t,s$ and whose restriction along addition on directions represents $r$. Define $\operatorname{Inf}_X$ to be the actual automorphisms of $X\times_KD_K$ preserving its projection to $D_K$ and restricting to the identity on the canonical marked copy of $X$; the projection to $X$ is not required to be fixed. Its scalar relation $\beta=c\alpha$ means the pullback of $\alpha$ under the canonical scaling map of the trivial family: that map is fixed by its projections (identity on the $X$-projection and scaling on the $D_K$-projection), and the pulled-back automorphism is fixed by its $X$-projection after that map and by its unchanged $D_K$-projection. These are definitions of the objects and operation relations, without asserting their vector-space laws or finite-dimensionality.
